newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain eases drought fear for French grain - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: Rain eases drought fear for French grain - ONIC.

text.p: Recent rains have eased concerns over France's grain crop but this month's rainfall will be crucial, national grain office ONIC said on Wednesday.

Despite nearly four months of drought until the end of April, soft wheat in the main production basins north of the Loire river escaped unscathed but barley yields may be below last year's, agency officials told a news conference.
Rain earlier this month came too late to contain damage to winter grain in the far south, where yields may fall by between 20 and 30 percent, ONIC official Michel Ferret said.
However the region is not a major grain area, making up less than 10 percent of the total acreage sown in France.
In the Dijon area in eastern France night frost hit barley crops, threatening to drive up protein content, Ferret, head of ONIC's international affairs division, told reporters.
High protein content makes barley unsuitable for malting as maltsters usually favour protein content below 11.5 percent.
In the Orleans area, at the heart of France's grain belt, yield potential for wheat and barley was left mainly intact.
"We avoided the worst for barley," Ferret said.
In southern France, the drought had "more marked, more irreversible consequences," Ferret said. The rain had had And little beneficial impact as it came with drying winds.
In other areas the situation was more mixed.
In Clermont Ferrand, central France, soft wheat yields could fall to four tonnes a hectare from six tonnes. Barley could drop to 3.5 tonnes from the same level.
For spring crops, recent rain had allowed farmers to get on with sowings and helped maize growth.
"We are coming out of the pessimistic stage, even if there is still drought in the south," ONIC director general Alain Moulinier said.
Increases in grain area and rain in northern France gave the country the chance to be "operational" with another reasonable crop this year, he said.
ONIC says the total area sown to grain has risen 3.38 percent to 8.99 million hectares for this year's harvest.
